IG14: Electronic Signature Service Implementation

IDEHA-IG-SVC-SIG-001 Version: 0.1

IDEHA-IG-OBJ-TST-001 Electronic Timestamp Implementation

Subject matter and scope

Article 1

  1. This Guideline lays down implementation requirements for Electronic Timestamps and Qualified Electronic Timestamps within the Trust Framework.

  2. This Guideline applies to Actors creating, managing, validating or relying upon Electronic Timestamps within the scope established by the applicable Framework Instruments.

  3. This Guideline establishes requirements for:

  1. Electronic Timestamp object identification;

  2. binding of electronic data to an identified time;

  3. timestamp evidence;

  4. timestamp object lifecycle management;

  5. dependencies required for Validation;

  6. Qualified Electronic Timestamp object conditions.

  1. This Guideline applies together with:

  1. IDEHA-IG-SVC-TST-001 Electronic Timestamp Service Implementation;

  2. IDEHA-IG-SVC-VVS-001 Validation and Verification Service Implementation;

  3. IDEHA-IG-OBJ-DSG-001 Digital Signature Creation Data and Device Implementation;

  4. IDEHA-IG-SEC-CRY-001 Cryptographic Controls and Cryptographic Agility Implementation;

  5. IDEHA-IG-ASR-GEN-001 Assurance, Conformity Assessment and Qualification Implementation.

  1. This Guideline does not establish:

  1. Electronic Timestamp Service operation;

  2. Trust Service Provider requirements;

  3. time-source operation procedures;

  4. clock synchronisation architecture;

  5. cryptographic algorithm selection;

  6. timestamp transport protocols;

  7. signature format timestamp integration.

Those matters shall be implemented through the applicable Framework Instruments.

Electronic Timestamp scope

Article 2

  1. An Electronic Timestamp shall establish a binding between identified electronic data and an identified time.

  2. The Electronic Timestamp shall identify:

  1. the referenced electronic data or data representation;

  2. the generated time value;

  3. the Timestamp Issuer;

  4. the applicable Timestamp Profile;

  5. the protection mechanism.

  1. The Electronic Timestamp shall remain associated with the referenced electronic data throughout its lifecycle.

Article 3

  1. The applicable Timestamp Profile shall define:

  1. the purpose of the Electronic Timestamp;

  2. the data reference method;

  3. the required time accuracy;

  4. the required evidence;

  5. the applicable Validation conditions;

  6. the applicable Security Conditions.

  1. A Timestamp Profile shall not modify the Electronic Timestamp Category or Controlled Effects established by the Main Framework.

Timestamp data binding

Article 4

  1. An Electronic Timestamp shall identify the electronic data to which the time value applies.

  2. The data binding shall enable determination of:

  1. the referenced electronic data;

  2. the applied data representation;

  3. the time value;

  4. the Timestamp Issuer;

  5. the applicable Profile.

  1. The Electronic Timestamp shall not require disclosure of the original electronic data where a protected data reference is used.

Article 5

  1. Where a digest or equivalent data reference is used, the applicable Technical Specification shall define:

  1. the data-reference representation;

  2. the permitted cryptographic mechanisms;

  3. the encoding;

  4. interoperability requirements.

  1. A digest or data reference shall not by itself establish the legal meaning, ownership or validity of the referenced data.

Time information

Article 6

  1. An Electronic Timestamp shall contain or reference an identified time value.

  2. The time information shall identify, where applicable:

  1. generation time;

  2. time precision;

  3. time accuracy;

  4. applicable time reference;

  5. uncertainty information.

  1. The interpretation of time information shall be defined by the applicable Timestamp Profile.

Article 7

  1. The Electronic Timestamp shall provide evidence sufficient to determine the relationship between:

  1. the referenced electronic data;

  2. the identified time;

  3. the Timestamp Issuer;

  4. the applicable Timestamp Profile.

  1. Timestamp evidence shall remain available for Validation according to the applicable lifecycle requirements.

Timestamp protection

Article 8

  1. An Electronic Timestamp shall be protected against unauthorised alteration.

  2. Protection mechanisms shall ensure:

  1. integrity of the timestamp information;

  2. authenticity of the Timestamp Issuer;

  3. detection of modification.

  1. The protection mechanism shall remain separate from the Timestamp Category.

Article 9

  1. Where an Electronic Timestamp depends on another Trust Object, the dependency shall be identified.

  2. Dependencies may include:

  1. Certificate;

  2. Electronic Signature;

  3. Electronic Seal;

  4. Trust List information;

  5. other Validation evidence.

  1. A dependency shall not transfer its Status, Qualified Status or Controlled Effects to the Electronic Timestamp.

Qualified Electronic Timestamp

Article 10

  1. A Qualified Electronic Timestamp shall satisfy the requirements established by the Main Framework and the applicable Qualified Object Profile.

  2. The Qualified Object Profile shall identify:

  1. required Qualified Trust Service Provider Status;

  2. required Qualified Trust Service Status;

  3. required time conditions;

  4. required protection conditions;

  5. required Validation conditions;

  6. required evidence.

  1. Qualification of the Electronic Timestamp Service shall not automatically qualify every Electronic Timestamp issued by that service.

  2. Qualified Status shall apply only where all applicable qualified conditions are satisfied.

Validation support

Article 11

  1. An Electronic Timestamp shall support Validation according to the applicable Validation requirements.

  2. Validation support shall enable determination of:

  1. timestamp integrity;

  2. Timestamp Issuer identity;

  3. referenced data binding;

  4. time information;

  5. protection validity;

  6. Status information;

  7. Historical State.

  1. Validation requirements shall be implemented through the Validation and Verification Service Implementation.

Article 12

  1. An Electronic Timestamp shall not by itself establish:

  1. ownership of the referenced data;

  2. legal validity of the referenced data;

  3. Authorisation;

  4. approval;

  5. consent;

  6. any fact expressed by the referenced data.

  1. Reliance upon an Electronic Timestamp shall consider:

  1. purpose;

  2. Profile;

  3. Status;

  4. Validation Result;

  5. applicable Reliance Conditions.

Timestamp lifecycle

Article 13

  1. The lifecycle of an Electronic Timestamp shall include, where applicable:

  1. creation;

  2. issuance;

  3. Validation;

  4. preservation;

  5. historical evaluation.

  1. Lifecycle information affecting reliance shall be recorded.

Article 14

  1. Changes affecting Electronic Timestamp dependencies shall be assessed where they may affect:

  1. integrity;

  2. Validation;

  3. Historical State;

  4. Controlled Reliance.

  1. The assessment shall identify:

  1. affected Electronic Timestamps;

  2. affected Certificates;

  3. affected cryptographic dependencies;

  4. applicable transition measures.

Preservation and long-term reliance

Article 15

  1. Where long-term reliance is required, the Electronic Timestamp shall support preservation of evidence necessary for Historical Validation.

  2. Preservation evidence may include:

  1. timestamp evidence;

  2. Certificate information;

  3. Status information;

  4. Validation evidence;

  5. cryptographic transition information.

  1. Long-term preservation requirements shall be defined by the applicable Profile.

Records and evidence

Article 16

  1. The responsible Actor shall maintain records sufficient to reconstruct:

  1. timestamp creation;

  2. referenced data binding;

  3. Timestamp Issuer;

  4. timestamp dependencies;

  5. lifecycle events;

  6. Validation history.

  1. Records shall be protected according to applicable Security Conditions.

Applicable standards

Article 17

  1. The standards applicable to this Guideline are set out in Annex I.

  2. A standard referenced in Annex I shall apply only for the implementation function identified in that Annex.

  3. Conformity with a referenced standard shall constitute evidence only for the requirements mapped to that standard.

  4. A referenced standard shall not create:

  1. Electronic Timestamp Category;

  2. Qualified Electronic Timestamp Status;

  3. Controlled Effects.

Annex I

Applicable standards

Reference Application
ETSI EN 319 422 Timestamp token and protocol profile requirements
RFC 3161 Time-Stamp Protocol
RFC 5816 ESSCertIDv2 update for timestamp token certificate identification
RFC 5280 Certificate validation where timestamp certificates are used
ETSI EN 319 102-1 Validation process requirements applicable to timestamps
ISO/IEC 18014-4 Traceability of time sources where applicable
ISO 8601-1:2019 Date and time representation

IDEHA-IG-SVC-TSP-001: Trust Service Provider and Trust Service Common Implementation

Version: 0.1

Subject matter and scope

Article 1

  1. This Guideline lays down implementation requirements applicable to Trust Service Providers and Trust Services operating under the Trust Framework.

  2. This Guideline applies to Trust Service Providers responsible for providing one or more Trust Services within the scope established by the applicable Framework Instruments.

  3. This Guideline establishes common implementation requirements for:

  1. Trust Service Provider governance;

  2. Trust Service inventory and separation;

  3. Trust Service operational management;

  4. service documentation and evidence;

  5. service lifecycle management;

  6. common security and continuity arrangements;

  7. dependencies between Trust Services.

  1. This Guideline applies together with the applicable Trust Service-specific Implementation Guideline.

  2. This Guideline does not establish:

  1. Trust Service Categories;

  2. Trust Service Provider Status;

  3. Qualified Trust Service Provider Status;

  4. Qualified Trust Service Status;

  5. Service Permission;

  6. Qualification decisions;

  7. Humanitarian Trust List governance;

  8. service-specific technical requirements.

Those matters shall be implemented through the applicable Framework Instruments.

Trust Service Provider operational identity

Article 2

  1. A Trust Service Provider shall maintain operational information identifying its Trust Service Provider functions.

  2. The operational information shall identify:

  1. Trust Service Provider Identifier;

  2. organisational information;

  3. applicable Provider Scope;

  4. responsible governance functions;

  5. provided Trust Services;

  6. applicable Service Permissions;

  7. lifecycle information.

  1. The Trust Service Provider Identifier shall remain separate from:

  1. Trust Service Identifier;

  2. Certificate Identifier;

  3. Service Digital Identity;

  4. Trust Object Identifier.

Trust Service inventory and separation

Article 3

  1. A Trust Service Provider shall maintain an inventory of Trust Services provided under the Trust Framework.

  2. The Trust Service inventory shall identify:

  1. Trust Service Identifier;

  2. Trust Service Category;

  3. Service Scope;

  4. applicable Profiles;

  5. applicable Technical Specifications;

  6. applicable Standards;

  7. operational Status.

  1. Each Trust Service shall remain separately identifiable.

  2. A Trust Service Provider shall not:

  1. merge separate Trust Services into one service identity;

  2. use one Service Identifier for different Trust Services;

  3. assume that qualification of one Trust Service applies to another Trust Service.

Article 4

  1. A Trust Service Provider providing multiple Trust Services shall maintain separation between:

  1. service governance;

  2. service operation;

  3. service evidence;

  4. service dependencies;

  5. service lifecycle.

  1. The separation shall be sufficient to determine the scope of each Trust Service independently.

Trust Service documentation

Article 5

  1. A Trust Service Provider shall maintain documentation necessary for operation and reliance upon each Trust Service.

  2. The documentation shall identify, where applicable:

  1. Trust Service description;

  2. Service Scope;

  3. applicable Profiles;

  4. applicable Technical Specifications;

  5. applicable Standards;

  6. operational limitations;

  7. security conditions;

  8. evidence requirements.

  1. Service documentation shall remain consistent with the applicable Framework Instruments.

Article 6

  1. A Trust Service Provider shall maintain service practice information sufficient to demonstrate how each Trust Service is operated.

  2. The practice information shall include, where applicable:

  1. responsibilities;

  2. operational procedures;

  3. security controls;

  4. incident handling arrangements;

  5. continuity arrangements;

  6. evidence retention requirements.

  1. Service practice information shall not modify requirements established by the Main Framework or applicable Profiles.

Trust Service operation

Article 7

  1. A Trust Service Provider shall operate each Trust Service within its assigned Service Scope.

  2. The Trust Service Provider shall ensure that each Trust Service:

  1. performs only permitted functions;

  2. applies applicable Profiles;

  3. applies applicable Technical Specifications;

  4. maintains required evidence;

  5. supports applicable Validation requirements.

  1. A Trust Service Provider shall not perform functions outside the approved scope of a Trust Service.

Article 8

  1. A Trust Service Provider shall maintain records of Trust Service operations.

  2. Operational records shall identify, where applicable:

  1. service requests;

  2. service outputs;

  3. processing events;

  4. Status changes;

  5. security events;

  6. lifecycle events.

  1. Operational records shall enable reconstruction of relevant service activities.

Dependencies and supporting functions

Article 9

  1. A Trust Service Provider shall identify dependencies required for operation of each Trust Service.

  2. Dependencies may include:

  1. Sources;

  2. Trust Objects;

  3. Certificates;

  4. Validation Services;

  5. Electronic Timestamp Services;

  6. Cryptographic mechanisms;

  7. supporting Actors.

  1. Dependency information shall identify:

  1. dependency purpose;

  2. applicable scope;

  3. required Status;

  4. applicable Validation conditions.

  1. A dependency shall not transfer its Status or Qualified Status to the Trust Service.

Security and confidentiality

Article 10

  1. A Trust Service Provider shall implement security measures appropriate to the Trust Services provided.

  2. Security measures shall address, where applicable:

  1. confidentiality;

  2. integrity;

  3. availability;

  4. authenticity;

  5. accountability;

  6. access control;

  7. monitoring.

  1. Security requirements specific to a Trust Service shall be established by the applicable Trust Service-specific Implementation Guideline.

Personnel and supporting Actors

Article 11

  1. A Trust Service Provider shall define responsibilities for persons and supporting Actors involved in Trust Service operation.

  2. Responsibilities shall identify:

  1. assigned functions;

  2. access permissions;

  3. competence requirements;

  4. segregation requirements;

  5. accountability arrangements.

  1. Supporting Actors shall operate only within the scope assigned by the Trust Service Provider.

Incident response and continuity

Article 12

  1. A Trust Service Provider shall maintain arrangements for:

  1. incident detection;

  2. incident response;

  3. service continuity;

  4. Recovery;

  5. evidence preservation.

  1. Incident and continuity arrangements shall identify:

  1. responsible functions;

  2. notification conditions;

  3. affected Trust Services;

  4. Recovery conditions.

  1. Service-specific incident requirements shall be established by the applicable Implementation Guideline.

Trust Service lifecycle management

Article 13

  1. A Trust Service Provider shall manage the lifecycle of each Trust Service.

  2. The lifecycle shall include, where applicable:

  1. preparation;

  2. activation;

  3. operation;

  4. modification;

  5. restriction;

  6. Suspension;

  7. withdrawal;

  8. cessation.

  1. Lifecycle changes shall be recorded.

Article 14

  1. Before implementing a material change affecting a Trust Service, the Trust Service Provider shall assess:

  1. affected Service Scope;

  2. affected Profiles;

  3. affected Technical Specifications;

  4. affected Standards;

  5. affected dependencies;

  6. impact on reliance.

  1. Material changes shall be managed according to the applicable Change Control requirements.

Qualification support

Article 15

  1. Where a Trust Service Provider seeks Qualified Status for a Trust Service, it shall prepare evidence according to the applicable Qualified Profile.

  2. Evidence shall identify:

  1. Trust Service scope;

  2. applicable requirements;

  3. conformity evidence;

  4. assessment results;

  5. limitations.

  1. Preparation of qualification evidence shall not create Qualified Status.

  2. Qualified Status shall arise only through the applicable Framework decision route.

Records and evidence

Article 16

  1. A Trust Service Provider shall maintain records sufficient to reconstruct:

  1. Trust Service establishment;

  2. service operation;

  3. service dependencies;

  4. service changes;

  5. security events;

  6. qualification evidence where applicable.

  1. Records shall be protected according to applicable Security Conditions.

Applicable standards

Article 17

  1. The standards applicable to this Guideline are set out in Annex I.

  2. A standard referenced in Annex I shall apply only for the implementation function identified in that Annex.

  3. Conformity with a referenced standard shall constitute evidence only for the requirements mapped to that standard.

  4. A referenced standard shall not create:

  1. Trust Service Category;

  2. Trust Service Status;

  3. Qualified Trust Service Status;

  4. Controlled Effects.

Annex I

Applicable standards

Reference Application
ETSI EN 319 401 General policy requirements for Trust Service Providers
ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Information security management controls applicable to Trust Service operation
ISO/IEC 27002:2022 Security control implementation guidance
ISO/IEC 27701:2025 Privacy information management where personal data processing is performed
ISO 22301:2019 Business continuity management where continuity requirements apply
ISO/IEC 20000-1:2018 Service management controls where service-management processes are applied

IDEHA-IG-SVC-IDN-001: Identification Service Implementation

Version: 0.1

Subject matter and scope

Article 1

  1. This Guideline lays down implementation requirements for Identification Services operating under the Trust Framework.

  2. This Guideline applies to Trust Service Providers providing Identification Services and Actors performing Identification Service functions within the applicable Service Scope.

  3. This Guideline establishes requirements for:

  1. Identity Proofing;

  2. Identity Registration;

  3. maintenance of Identity Registration Records;

  4. Identifier allocation and management;

  5. Identity Resolution;

  6. identity lifecycle management;

  7. Identification Results.

  1. This Guideline applies together with:

  1. IDEHA-IG-SRC-ASO-001 Source and Authoritative Source Implementation;

  2. IDEHA-IG-DAT-SEM-001 Controlled Data Elements, Semantics and Data Quality Implementation;

  3. IDEHA-IG-BIO-GEN-001 Biometric Implementation Controls;

  4. IDEHA-IG-SVC-AUT-001 Authentication Service Implementation;

  5. IDEHA-IG-SVC-EAS-001 Electronic Attestation Service Implementation;

  6. IDEHA-IG-ASR-GEN-001 Assurance, Conformity Assessment and Qualification Implementation.

  1. This Guideline does not establish:

  1. civil registration authority;

  2. legal identity creation;

  3. Source authority;

  4. Electronic Attestation issuance;

  5. Authentication Service operation;

  6. Authorisation decisions;

  7. biometric technical formats;

  8. technical data exchange protocols.

Those matters shall be implemented through the applicable Framework Instruments.

Identification Service scope

Article 2

  1. An Identification Service shall operate within an identified Service Scope.

  2. The Service Scope shall identify:

  1. Subject categories;

  2. permitted Identification Service Functions;

  3. applicable Sources;

  4. applicable Profiles;

  5. applicable Assurance Conditions;

  6. applicable Security Conditions;

  7. applicable jurisdictions or operational domains.

  1. An Identification Service shall not perform functions outside its approved Service Scope.

Article 3

  1. The Identification Service shall distinguish between:

  1. identity evidence;

  2. identity information;

  3. Identity Registration Records;

  4. Identification Results;

  5. Identity Resolution Results.

  1. The Identification Service shall maintain separation between:

  1. the registered identity representation;

  2. the evidence used to establish that representation;

  3. the Source providing the evidence;

  4. outputs produced by the Identification Service.

Identity Proofing

Article 4

  1. Identity Proofing shall establish confidence that identity information relates to the identified Subject.

  2. Identity Proofing shall evaluate:

  1. identity evidence;

  2. Source information;

  3. biographic information;

  4. biometric information where applicable;

  5. demographic information where applicable;

  6. other permitted evidence.

  1. The applicable Profile shall define:

  1. accepted evidence types;

  2. evidence quality requirements;

  3. verification methods;

  4. assurance conditions;

  5. failure and exception handling.

Article 5

  1. The Identification Service shall record evidence supporting an Identity Proofing result.

  2. The evidence record shall identify, where applicable:

  1. evidence type;

  2. evidence Source;

  3. collection method;

  4. verification method;

  5. processing time;

  6. responsible Actor;

  7. outcome.

  1. Evidence used for Identity Proofing shall remain attributable to its Source and shall not become a new Source solely through use by the Identification Service.

Identity Registration

Article 6

  1. Identity Registration shall establish and maintain an Identity Registration Record for a registered Subject.

  2. An Identity Registration Record shall contain or reference, where applicable:

  1. biographic data;

  2. biometric data;

  3. demographic data;

  4. allocated Identification Number;

  5. family relationship information;

  6. contact details;

  7. identification document details;

  8. registration evidence;

  9. lifecycle information.

  1. The applicable Profile shall define the permitted data elements, retention conditions and reuse conditions.

Article 7

  1. The Identification Service shall ensure that Identity Registration Records maintain:

  1. provenance;

  2. Data Quality information;

  3. Source references;

  4. correction history;

  5. lifecycle information.

  1. Information contained in an Identity Registration Record shall remain distinguishable according to its origin and purpose.

  2. Derived information shall identify:

  1. source information;

  2. derivation method;

  3. responsible processing function;

  4. applicable Version.

Identification Number

Article 8

  1. An Identification Service assigning an Identification Number shall maintain an Identifier namespace.

  2. An Identification Number shall:

  1. uniquely identify the Subject within the applicable namespace;

  2. remain stable during the applicable lifecycle;

  3. remain separate from identity Attributes;

  4. remain separate from Trust Object Identifiers.

  1. An Identification Number shall not:

  1. disclose identity type;

  2. disclose demographic information;

  3. disclose jurisdictional meaning unless required by the identifier scheme;

  4. encode Status or qualification information.

  1. The applicable Profile shall define:

  1. generation method;

  2. uniqueness scope;

  3. non-reuse conditions;

  4. lifecycle treatment.

Identity Resolution

Article 9

  1. Identity Resolution shall determine whether identity information refers to:

  1. an existing Identity Registration Record;

  2. a different Identity Registration Record;

  3. an unresolved identity state.

  1. Identity Resolution shall consider:

  1. available identity information;

  2. applicable matching rules;

  3. permitted biometric comparison where applicable;

  4. confidence thresholds;

  5. human review requirements.

  1. Identity Resolution shall not create a legal identity or alter Source records.

Article 10

  1. Where automated matching is used, the Identification Service shall maintain evidence of:

  1. matching method;

  2. algorithm Version;

  3. thresholds;

  4. input data;

  5. result;

  6. limitations.

  1. The applicable Profile shall define requirements for:

  1. false match risk;

  2. false non-match risk;

  3. demographic performance;

  4. human review.

Biographic, biometric and demographic data

Article 11

  1. The Identification Service shall process biographic, biometric and demographic data according to the applicable Profile.

  2. The applicable Profile shall identify:

  1. permitted data elements;

  2. collection conditions;

  3. Source requirements;

  4. quality requirements;

  5. retention conditions;

  6. reuse conditions.

  1. Biometric data shall be processed according to the applicable Biometric Implementation requirements.

  2. Demographic data shall remain separate from:

  1. Identification Number;

  2. Subject Identifier;

  3. Trust Object Identifier.

Identity Registration Record lifecycle

Article 12

  1. The Identification Service shall manage the lifecycle of Identity Registration Records.

  2. Lifecycle management shall include, where applicable:

  1. creation;

  2. update;

  3. correction;

  4. suspension;

  5. recovery;

  6. closure;

  7. historical preservation.

  1. Lifecycle events shall identify:

  1. responsible Actor;

  2. effective time;

  3. reason;

  4. supporting evidence.

Article 13

  1. Corrections to Identity Registration Records shall preserve sufficient evidence to reconstruct:

  1. previous information;

  2. correction basis;

  3. responsible Actor;

  4. effective time.

  1. A correction shall not remove historical information required for accountability or Historical State determination.

Identification Results

Article 14

  1. An Identification Service shall produce an Identification Result where an Identification Service Function produces an outcome intended for use by another Actor.

  2. An Identification Result shall identify, where applicable:

  1. Subject reference;

  2. Identification Service;

  3. evaluated evidence basis;

  4. Assurance Conditions;

  5. evaluation time;

  6. limitations.

  1. An Identification Result shall not:

  1. create legal identity;

  2. create Source authority;

  3. create Authorisation;

  4. create entitlement.

Article 15

  1. An Identity Resolution Result shall identify, where applicable:

  1. evaluated records;

  2. resolution method;

  3. confidence information;

  4. limitations;

  5. evaluation time.

  1. An Identity Resolution Result shall remain separate from an Identification Result.

Reuse and disclosure

Article 16

  1. Identity Registration Record information shall be reused only within the conditions established by the applicable Profile.

  2. Reuse conditions shall consider:

  1. purpose;

  2. Service Scope;

  3. Source Basis;

  4. Freshness Condition;

  5. Assurance Conditions;

  6. disclosure restrictions.

  1. The Identification Service shall not disclose Identity Registration Record information beyond the authorised scope.

Security and safeguards

Article 17

  1. The Identification Service shall protect Identity Registration Records and related evidence against:

  1. unauthorised access;

  2. unauthorised modification;

  3. unauthorised disclosure;

  4. loss of integrity.

  1. Access shall be controlled through:

  1. Authentication;

  2. Authorisation;

  3. purpose restrictions;

  4. audit requirements.

  1. Protected-Person Safeguards and Accessible Alternatives shall apply where required.

Records and evidence

Article 18

  1. The Identification Service shall maintain records sufficient to reconstruct:

  1. Identity Proofing;

  2. Identity Registration;

  3. Identity Resolution;

  4. Identifier allocation;

  5. corrections;

  6. lifecycle changes;

  7. Identification Results.

  1. Records shall identify:

  1. responsible Actor;

  2. Source Basis;

  3. processing method;

  4. applicable Profile Version.

Applicable standards

Article 19

  1. The standards applicable to this Guideline are set out in Annex I.

  2. A standard referenced in Annex I shall apply only for the implementation function identified in that Annex.

  3. Conformity with a referenced standard shall constitute evidence only for the requirements mapped to that standard.

  4. A referenced standard shall not create:

  1. identity;

  2. Source authority;

  3. Identification Service Status;

  4. Controlled Effects.

Annex I

IDEHA-IG-SVC-AUT-001: Authentication Service Implementation

Version: 0.1

Subject matter and scope

Article 1

  1. This Guideline lays down implementation requirements for Authentication Services operating under the Trust Framework.

  2. This Guideline applies to Trust Service Providers providing Authentication Services and Actors performing Authentication functions within the applicable Service Scope.

  3. This Guideline establishes requirements for:

  1. Subject Authentication;

  2. System Authentication;

  3. Authentication Mechanisms;

  4. Authenticators;

  5. Authentication Events;

  6. Authentication Outcomes;

  7. session and reauthentication management.

  1. This Guideline applies together with:

  1. IDEHA-IG-SVC-IDN-001 Identification Service Implementation;

  2. IDEHA-IG-SVC-AUZ-001 Authorisation Service Implementation;

  3. IDEHA-IG-OBJ-DSG-001 Digital Signature Creation Data and Device Implementation where cryptographic Authenticators are used;

  4. IDEHA-IG-SEC-CRY-001 Cryptographic Controls and Cryptographic Agility Implementation;

  5. IDEHA-IG-BIO-GEN-001 Biometric Implementation Controls where biometric Authenticators are used;

  6. IDEHA-IG-ASR-GEN-001 Assurance, Conformity Assessment and Qualification Implementation.

  1. This Guideline does not establish:

  1. identity;

  2. Identity Proofing;

  3. Identity Registration;

  4. Authorisation;

  5. Electronic Signature;

  6. Electronic Seal;

  7. Trust Object issuance;

  8. access policy decisions;

  9. cryptographic algorithm selection.

Those matters shall be implemented through the applicable Framework Instruments.

Authentication Service scope

Article 2

  1. An Authentication Service shall operate within an identified Service Scope.

  2. The Service Scope shall identify:

  1. authenticated Subject or entity categories;

  2. permitted Authentication Mechanisms;

  3. supported Authenticators;

  4. applicable Assurance Conditions;

  5. applicable Security Conditions;

  6. applicable Profiles;

  7. applicable Technical Specifications.

  1. An Authentication Service shall not perform functions outside its approved Service Scope.

Article 3

  1. An Authentication Service shall distinguish between:

  1. Authentication;

  2. Authentication Mechanism;

  3. Authenticator;

  4. Authentication Event;

  5. Authentication Outcome.

  1. The Authentication Service shall maintain separation between:

  1. identity information used for Authentication;

  2. Authentication evidence;

  3. Authentication decision;

  4. Authorisation decision.

  1. A successful Authentication Event shall not by itself create Authorisation.

Authentication Mechanisms

Article 4

  1. An Authentication Service shall use Authentication Mechanisms appropriate to the applicable Assurance Conditions.

  2. An Authentication Mechanism shall define:

  1. authenticated entity;

  2. authentication method;

  3. required inputs;

  4. required evidence;

  5. security conditions;

  6. failure conditions.

  1. The applicable Authentication Profile shall specify:

  1. permitted mechanisms;

  2. assurance level;

  3. factor requirements;

  4. replay resistance requirements;

  5. phishing resistance requirements where applicable.

Article 5

  1. Authentication Mechanisms may include:

  1. knowledge factors;

  2. possession factors;

  3. inherence factors;

  4. cryptographic Authenticators;

  5. device-based Authenticators;

  6. service or system authentication mechanisms.

  1. The applicable Profile shall determine the permitted combination of factors.

  2. A biometric characteristic shall not by itself constitute an Authenticator unless explicitly permitted by the applicable Profile.

Authenticators

Article 6

  1. An Authenticator shall be uniquely associated with the authenticated Subject or entity within the applicable scope.

  2. Authenticator information shall identify:

  1. Authenticator Identifier;

  2. associated Subject or entity reference;

  3. Authenticator type;

  4. activation conditions;

  5. lifecycle Status;

  6. effective period.

  1. An Authenticator Identifier shall:

  1. remain opaque;

  2. not disclose identity type;

  3. not disclose personal information;

  4. remain separate from Subject Identifier and Trust Object Identifier.

Article 7

  1. The Authentication Service shall manage the Authenticator lifecycle.

  2. Lifecycle management shall include:

  1. issuance;

  2. binding;

  3. activation;

  4. use;

  5. suspension;

  6. replacement;

  7. revocation;

  8. recovery;

  9. termination.

  1. Lifecycle events affecting Authentication assurance shall be recorded.

Subject Authentication

Article 8

  1. Subject Authentication shall determine whether the identified Subject successfully demonstrates control of an approved Authenticator.

  2. Subject Authentication shall evaluate:

  1. Authentication request;

  2. Authenticator status;

  3. Authentication mechanism;

  4. required factors;

  5. security conditions.

  1. Subject Authentication shall not establish:

  1. identity;

  2. legal capacity;

  3. entitlement;

  4. Authorisation.

Article 9

  1. Where Subject Authentication uses a cryptographic Authenticator, the Authentication Service shall verify:

  1. possession or control of the cryptographic material;

  2. integrity of the Authentication response;

  3. freshness of the Authentication Event;

  4. applicable certificate or key status where relevant.

  1. Cryptographic key lifecycle requirements shall be established through the applicable Cryptographic Controls requirements.

System Authentication

Article 10

  1. System Authentication shall determine whether a system, service, device or Endpoint is authenticated within the applicable scope.

  2. System Authentication may apply to:

  1. information systems;

  2. services;

  3. applications;

  4. devices;

  5. workloads;

  6. gateways;

  7. Endpoints.

  1. System Authentication shall identify:

  1. authenticated system or entity;

  2. authentication mechanism;

  3. credential or certificate reference;

  4. Authentication Event;

  5. applicable Security Conditions.

Article 11

  1. A system Authentication Credential shall remain separate from:

  1. Subject Authentication credentials;

  2. Authorisation credentials;

  3. Trust Service Identifier;

  4. Trust Object Identifier.

  1. A system successfully authenticated shall not automatically receive permission to access a resource.

  2. Authorisation shall be determined through the applicable Authorisation Service.

Biometric Authentication

Article 12

  1. Where biometric information contributes to Authentication, the Authentication Service shall apply the applicable Biometric Implementation requirements.

  2. Biometric Authentication shall consider:

  1. biometric sample quality;

  2. biometric reference protection;

  3. presentation attack detection;

  4. applicable performance requirements;

  5. accessibility conditions.

  1. A biometric comparison result shall not independently establish identity or Authorisation.

Authentication Events

Article 13

  1. Each Authentication Event shall be uniquely identifiable within the applicable scope.

  2. An Authentication Event record shall identify:

  1. Authentication Event Identifier;

  2. authenticated Subject or entity;

  3. Authentication Mechanism;

  4. Authenticator used;

  5. Authentication time;

  6. result;

  7. Assurance Conditions achieved;

  8. limitations.

  1. Authentication Event information shall be protected according to applicable Security Conditions.

Article 14

  1. An Authentication Event shall remain associated with the conditions under which it occurred.

  2. The Authentication Service shall record:

  1. successful Authentication;

  2. failed Authentication;

  3. rejected Authentication;

  4. restricted Authentication;

  5. step-up Authentication where applicable.

  1. Authentication evidence shall be retained according to the applicable Profile.

Authentication Outcomes

Article 15

  1. An Authentication Service shall produce an Authentication Outcome following an Authentication Event.

  2. An Authentication Outcome shall identify:

  1. authenticated Subject or entity;

  2. Authentication Service;

  3. Authentication Mechanism;

  4. achieved Assurance Conditions;

  5. Authentication time;

  6. validity period;

  7. limitations.

  1. An Authentication Outcome shall remain separate from:

  1. Authorisation Outcome;

  2. Electronic Attestation;

  3. Electronic Signature.

Article 16

  1. An Authentication Outcome shall support Verification and Validation.

  2. Validation shall determine, where applicable:

  1. Authentication Service Status;

  2. Authenticator Status;

  3. Authentication Mechanism;

  4. Assurance Conditions;

  5. validity period;

  6. Historical State.

  1. An Authentication Outcome shall not establish Authorisation.

Session and reauthentication management

Article 17

  1. Where an Authentication Service establishes a session, the session shall be associated with the applicable Authentication Outcome.

  2. Session management shall define:

  1. session identifier;

  2. session validity period;

  3. inactivity conditions;

  4. reauthentication conditions;

  5. termination conditions.

  1. A session shall not provide a higher assurance level than the Authentication Event that established it.

Article 18

  1. Reauthentication shall be required where:

  1. the applicable Profile requires it;

  2. the session exceeds its permitted period;

  3. risk conditions change;

  4. the requested operation requires additional assurance.

  1. Step-up Authentication shall establish a new Authentication Outcome or update the existing outcome according to the applicable Profile.

Failure, recovery and replacement

Article 19

  1. The Authentication Service shall maintain procedures for:

  1. failed Authentication;

  2. Authenticator recovery;

  3. Authenticator replacement;

  4. compromised Authenticator handling.

  1. Recovery and replacement processes shall provide assurance equivalent to the intended Authentication use unless the applicable Profile establishes another condition.

Security and safeguards

Article 20

  1. The Authentication Service shall protect Authentication information against:

  1. unauthorised access;

  2. credential compromise;

  3. replay;

  4. impersonation;

  5. unauthorised disclosure.

  1. Security controls shall include, where applicable:

  1. monitoring;

  2. anomaly detection;

  3. rate limitation;

  4. audit records;

  5. incident response.

Records and evidence

Article 21

  1. The Authentication Service shall maintain records sufficient to reconstruct:

  1. Authentication Events;

  2. Authentication Outcomes;

  3. Authenticator lifecycle;

  4. failed Authentication attempts;

  5. recovery actions;

  6. security events.

  1. Records shall be protected according to applicable Security Conditions.

Applicable standards

Article 22

  1. The standards applicable to this Guideline are set out in Annex I.

  2. A standard referenced in Annex I shall apply only for the implementation function identified in that Annex.

  3. Conformity with a referenced standard shall constitute evidence only for the requirements mapped to that standard.

  4. A referenced standard shall not create:

  1. identity;

  2. Authorisation;

  3. Trust Object Status;

  4. Controlled Effects.

Annex I

Applicable standards

Reference Application
NIST SP 800-63B-4 Authentication and Authenticator management requirements
ISO/IEC 29115:2013 Entity Authentication Assurance framework
ISO/IEC 9798-1:2010 Entity Authentication framework
ISO/IEC 9798-2:2019 Symmetric cryptographic Authentication mechanisms
ISO/IEC 9798-3:2019 Public-key cryptographic Authentication mechanisms
RFC 5280 Certificate validation where certificate-based Authentication is used
RFC 9525 Service identity verification in TLS
RFC 8446 TLS 1.3 protected communication
ISO/IEC 24745:2022 Biometric information protection
ISO/IEC 30107-1:2023 Presentation attack detection framework
ISO/IEC 30107-3:2023 Presentation attack detection testing
ISO/IEC 19795-1:2021 Biometric performance testing

IDEHA-IG-SVC-AUZ-001: Authorisation Service Implementation

Version: 0.1

Subject matter and scope

Article 1

  1. This Guideline lays down implementation requirements for Authorisation Services operating under the Trust Framework.

  2. This Guideline applies to Trust Service Providers providing Authorisation Services and Actors performing Authorisation functions within the applicable Service Scope.

  3. This Guideline establishes requirements for:

  1. Authorisation Policy management;

  2. Authorisation request processing;

  3. policy evaluation;

  4. Authorisation decision generation;

  5. Authorisation Outcome management;

  6. enforcement coordination;

  7. lifecycle management of Authorisation decisions.

  1. This Guideline applies together with:

  1. IDEHA-IG-SVC-AUT-001 Authentication Service Implementation;

  2. IDEHA-IG-ACT-PAR-001 Participation, Roles, Mandates and Representation Implementation;

  3. IDEHA-IG-SRC-ASO-001 Source and Authoritative Source Implementation;

  4. IDEHA-IG-SVC-FDX-001 Federated Data Exchange Service Implementation where Authorisation applies to data exchange;

  5. IDEHA-IG-ASR-GEN-001 Assurance, Conformity Assessment and Qualification Implementation.

  1. This Guideline does not establish:

  1. identity;

  2. Authentication;

  3. Identity Proofing;

  4. Identity Registration;

  5. Source authority;

  6. legal rights or entitlements;

  7. data-sharing agreements;

  8. cryptographic mechanisms;

  9. access-token formats;

  10. protocol bindings.

Those matters shall be implemented through the applicable Framework Instruments.

Authorisation Service scope

Article 2

  1. An Authorisation Service shall operate within an identified Service Scope.

  2. The Service Scope shall identify:

  1. permitted Authorisation functions;

  2. Actor categories;

  3. Controlled Matters subject to evaluation;

  4. applicable Policies;

  5. applicable Profiles;

  6. applicable Assurance Conditions;

  7. applicable Security Conditions.

  1. An Authorisation Service shall not perform functions outside its approved Service Scope.

Article 3

  1. An Authorisation Service shall distinguish between:

  1. Authentication Outcome;

  2. Authorisation Request;

  3. Authorisation Policy;

  4. Authorisation Decision;

  5. Authorisation Outcome;

  6. Policy Enforcement.

  1. A successful Authentication Event shall not by itself establish Authorisation.

  2. An Authorisation Outcome shall not establish identity, Source authority, legal capacity or entitlement unless such matters are determined by another applicable Framework Instrument.

Authorisation architecture

Article 4

  1. An Authorisation Service shall maintain functions necessary for policy-based evaluation.

  2. The functions may include:

  1. Policy Administration Function;

  2. Policy Decision Function;

  3. Policy Information Function;

  4. Policy Enforcement Function.

  1. The applicable Profile shall define the functions required for each implementation context.

Article 5

  1. The Policy Administration Function shall manage Authorisation Policies.

  2. Policy administration shall include:

  1. creation;

  2. approval;

  3. publication;

  4. modification;

  5. suspension;

  6. withdrawal;

  7. version management.

  1. Policy administration shall remain separate from Policy evaluation.

Authorisation Policies

Article 6

  1. An Authorisation Policy shall define conditions under which an Action may be permitted, denied or restricted.

  2. An Authorisation Policy shall identify, where applicable:

  1. Policy Identifier;

  2. Policy Version;

  3. Policy Owner;

  4. applicable Actors;

  5. Controlled Matters;

  6. permitted Actions;

  7. purposes;

  8. required Attributes;

  9. obligations;

  10. restrictions;

  11. validity period.

  1. An Authorisation Policy shall operate only within the scope assigned by the responsible Actor.

Article 7

  1. An Authorisation Policy shall not:

  1. create a Subject identity;

  2. create a Role;

  3. create a Mandate;

  4. create a Source authority;

  5. create a legal entitlement.

  1. Where a Policy requires Roles, Mandates, Attributes or Source information, those inputs shall be obtained from applicable authoritative functions.

Authorisation Request

Article 8

  1. An Authorisation Request shall identify the requested Action and the Controlled Matter to which the Action applies.

  2. An Authorisation Request shall contain, where applicable:

  1. requesting Actor;

  2. represented Subject where applicable;

  3. recipient;

  4. Controlled Matter;

  5. requested Action;

  6. Purpose;

  7. Authentication Outcome reference;

  8. Role or Mandate reference;

  9. applicable consent reference where applicable;

  10. contextual information.

  1. The applicable Technical Specification shall define the technical representation of Authorisation Requests.

Article 9

  1. Before evaluation, the Authorisation Service shall verify that the Authorisation Request is complete and within the Service Scope.

  2. The verification shall determine:

  1. presence of required information;

  2. validity of references;

  3. applicability of the requested Action;

  4. applicability of the requested Controlled Matter.

Policy evaluation

Article 10

  1. The Policy Decision Function shall evaluate the Authorisation Request against the applicable Authorisation Policy.

  2. The evaluation shall consider, where applicable:

  1. Actor Attributes;

  2. Subject Attributes;

  3. Role information;

  4. Mandate information;

  5. Source information;

  6. Authentication Assurance;

  7. Purpose;

  8. environmental conditions;

  9. security conditions.

  1. The evaluation result shall be recorded as an Authorisation Decision.

Article 11

  1. Where required information is unavailable, invalid or insufficient, the Authorisation Decision shall not result in an unauthorised Permit.

  2. The Authorisation Service shall identify, where applicable:

  1. missing information;

  2. unavailable Sources;

  3. expired conditions;

  4. unresolved conflicts;

  5. policy limitations.

  1. An inability to determine Authorisation shall remain distinguishable from a Deny decision.

Roles, Mandates and delegated authority

Article 12

  1. An Authorisation Service may evaluate Roles, Mandates and representation information as decision inputs.

  2. The evaluation shall determine:

  1. existence of the Role or Mandate;

  2. applicable scope;

  3. validity period;

  4. restrictions;

  5. relationship to the requested Action.

  1. A Role or Mandate used in an Authorisation decision shall not be expanded beyond its assigned scope.

Article 13

  1. A delegated authority shall be evaluated against:

  1. delegating Actor;

  2. delegated Actor;

  3. delegated scope;

  4. permitted Actions;

  5. validity period;

  6. revocation conditions.

  1. Delegation shall not permit an Actor to grant authority exceeding the authority available to that Actor.

Consent and purpose conditions

Article 14

  1. Where consent is applicable, the Authorisation Service may evaluate consent information as an Authorisation input.

  2. Consent information shall identify, where applicable:

  1. consenting Subject;

  2. receiving Actor;

  3. permitted data or Controlled Matter;

  4. purpose;

  5. validity period;

  6. withdrawal status;

  7. limitations.

  1. Consent shall remain separate from:

  1. Authentication;

  2. Authorisation Policy;

  3. Authorisation Outcome.

  1. The existence of consent shall not replace other required Authorisation conditions.

Authorisation Outcome

Article 15

  1. An Authorisation Service shall produce an Authorisation Outcome following evaluation.

  2. An Authorisation Outcome shall identify:

  1. Authorisation Outcome Identifier;

  2. requesting Actor;

  3. represented Subject where applicable;

  4. Controlled Matter;

  5. Action;

  6. Purpose;

  7. decision;

  8. Policy Identifier and Version;

  9. evaluation time;

  10. validity period;

  11. obligations;

  12. restrictions;

  13. limitations.

  1. An Authorisation Outcome shall remain separate from:

  1. Authentication Outcome;

  2. Electronic Attestation;

  3. Electronic Signature;

  4. Authorisation Policy.

Article 16

  1. An Authorisation Outcome may contain obligations requiring enforcement by another Actor or function.

  2. Obligations may include:

  1. restricted disclosure;

  2. additional verification;

  3. logging;

  4. human approval;

  5. purpose limitation;

  6. retention restrictions.

  1. The Policy Enforcement Function shall verify that mandatory obligations can be satisfied before permitting the requested Action.

Policy Enforcement

Article 17

  1. Policy Enforcement shall apply the Authorisation Outcome to the requested operation.

  2. The Policy Enforcement Function shall verify:

  1. Outcome integrity;

  2. Outcome validity;

  3. applicable scope;

  4. obligations;

  5. restrictions.

  1. Policy Enforcement shall not modify the substantive Authorisation decision.

Continuous authorisation and re-evaluation

Article 18

  1. An Authorisation Outcome shall remain valid only for the conditions and period established by the applicable Policy.

  2. Re-evaluation shall occur where:

  1. the validity period expires;

  2. the Authentication Outcome changes;

  3. Role or Mandate information changes;

  4. Source Status changes;

  5. requested Action changes;

  6. Purpose changes;

  7. risk conditions materially change.

  1. A cached Authorisation Outcome shall not be used beyond its permitted scope.

Lifecycle management

Article 19

  1. The lifecycle of an Authorisation Outcome shall include, where applicable:

  1. creation;

  2. activation;

  3. use;

  4. expiry;

  5. revocation;

  6. replacement;

  7. historical retention.

  1. Lifecycle events shall identify:

  1. responsible Actor;

  2. effective time;

  3. reason;

  4. supporting evidence.

Security and records

Article 20

  1. The Authorisation Service shall protect:

  1. Authorisation Policies;

  2. Authorisation Requests;

  3. Authorisation Decisions;

  4. Authorisation Outcomes;

  5. evaluation evidence.

  1. Protection shall include:

  1. confidentiality;

  2. integrity;

  3. access control;

  4. accountability;

  5. auditability.

Article 21

  1. The Authorisation Service shall maintain records sufficient to reconstruct:

  1. evaluated Request;

  2. applicable Policy;

  3. decision inputs;

  4. Authorisation Decision;

  5. Authorisation Outcome;

  6. enforcement result.

  1. Records shall enable historical determination of the Authorisation conditions applicable at the relevant time.

Applicable standards

Article 22

  1. The standards applicable to this Guideline are set out in Annex I.

  2. A standard referenced in Annex I shall apply only for the implementation function identified in that Annex.

  3. Conformity with a referenced standard shall constitute evidence only for the requirements mapped to that standard.

  4. A referenced standard shall not create:

  1. identity;

  2. Authentication;

  3. Authorisation;

  4. Controlled Effects.

Annex I

Applicable standards

Reference Application
ISO/IEC 29146:2024 Access-management architecture and distributed authorisation functions
ISO/IEC 10181-3:1996 Access-control framework concepts
NIST SP 800-162 Attribute Based Access Control implementation guidance
OASIS XACML 3.0 Policy language and decision model

XACML REST Profile 1.1 REST-based policy decision interface
XACML RBAC Profile 1.0 Role-based policy evaluation where applicable

ISO/IEC 27701:2025 Privacy management controls where personal data access decisions are performed

IDEHA-IG-SVC-DSG-001: Digital Signing Service Implementation

Version: 0.1

Subject matter and scope

Article 1

  1. This Guideline lays down implementation requirements for Digital Signing Services operating under the Trust Framework.

  2. This Guideline applies to Trust Service Providers providing Digital Signing Services and Actors operating Digital Signing Service functions within the applicable Service Scope.

  3. This Guideline establishes requirements for:

  1. Digital Signing Service operation;

  2. signing request processing;

  3. Digital Signature creation orchestration;

  4. interaction with Digital Signature Creation Mechanisms and Devices;

  5. signing evidence management;

  6. service lifecycle management.

  1. This Guideline applies together with:

  1. IDEHA-IG-OBJ-DSG-001 Digital Signature Creation Data and Device Implementation;

  2. IDEHA-IG-OBJ-SIG-001 Electronic Signature Implementation;

  3. IDEHA-IG-OBJ-SEL-001 Electronic Seal Implementation where applicable;

  4. IDEHA-IG-SVC-AUT-001 Authentication Service Implementation;

  5. IDEHA-IG-SVC-AUZ-001 Authorisation Service Implementation;

  6. IDEHA-IG-SVC-VVS-001 Validation and Verification Service Implementation;

  7. IDEHA-IG-ASR-GEN-001 Assurance, Conformity Assessment and Qualification Implementation.

  1. This Guideline does not establish:

  1. Digital Signature Creation Data requirements;

  2. Digital Signature Creation Device requirements;

  3. Qualified Digital Signature Creation Device requirements;

  4. Electronic Signature requirements;

  5. Electronic Seal requirements;

  6. Signatory identification requirements;

  7. signing intent requirements;

  8. signature format requirements;

  9. cryptographic algorithm selection.

Those matters shall be implemented through the applicable Framework Instruments.

Digital Signing Service scope

Article 2

  1. A Digital Signing Service shall operate within an identified Service Scope.

  2. The Service Scope shall identify:

  1. permitted signing functions;

  2. supported Digital Signature Creation Mechanisms;

  3. supported Digital Signature Creation Devices;

  4. supported Signature Profiles;

  5. applicable Assurance Conditions;

  6. applicable Security Conditions;

  7. applicable Technical Specifications.

  1. A Digital Signing Service shall not perform signing operations outside its approved Service Scope.

Article 3

  1. A Digital Signing Service shall maintain separation between:

  1. signing request processing;

  2. Digital Signature creation;

  3. Electronic Signature creation;

  4. Electronic Seal creation;

  5. Validation activities.

  1. A Digital Signing Service shall create Digital Signatures only.

  2. The resulting Digital Signature shall become part of an Electronic Signature or Electronic Seal only through the applicable Framework Instrument.

Signing request processing

Article 4

  1. A Digital Signing Service shall process signing requests according to the applicable Signing Profile.

  2. A signing request shall identify, where applicable:

  1. requesting Actor;

  2. requested signing operation;

  3. data to be signed;

  4. Digital Signature Creation Mechanism;

  5. Digital Signature Creation Device;

  6. applicable Profile;

  7. required evidence.

  1. The Digital Signing Service shall verify that the requested operation is within its Service Scope.

Article 5

  1. Before creating a Digital Signature, the Digital Signing Service shall determine that:

  1. the request is valid;

  2. the required Digital Signature Creation Device is available;

  3. the Digital Signature Creation Data may be used;

  4. applicable Authentication conditions are satisfied;

  5. applicable Authorisation conditions are satisfied.

  1. The Digital Signing Service shall not determine:

  1. legal effect of the signed data;

  2. existence of signing intent;

  3. validity of the resulting Electronic Signature.

Those matters belong to the applicable Electronic Signature Profile.

Interaction with Digital Signature Creation Devices

Article 6

  1. A Digital Signing Service shall use Digital Signature Creation Mechanisms and Digital Signature Creation Devices according to the applicable Profile.

  2. The Digital Signing Service shall maintain evidence of:

  1. selected Digital Signature Creation Device;

  2. selected Digital Signature Creation Mechanism;

  3. signing operation;

  4. creation result;

  5. applicable configuration.

  1. The Digital Signing Service shall not alter the security boundary or evaluated configuration of a Digital Signature Creation Device.

Article 7

  1. Where a Digital Signing Service operates with a remote Digital Signature Creation Device, it shall ensure that:

  1. the correct signing operation is selected;

  2. the intended data representation is provided;

  3. communication with the device is protected;

  4. creation evidence is generated.

  1. Remote operation shall comply with the applicable remote signing Profile.

  2. The Digital Signing Service shall not replace the requirements applicable to the Digital Signature Creation Device.

Authentication and Authorisation dependencies

Article 8

  1. Where required by the applicable Profile, a Digital Signing Service shall require an Authentication Outcome before initiating a signing operation.

  2. The Authentication Outcome shall identify, where applicable:

  1. authenticated Subject;

  2. Authentication Service;

  3. Authentication Assurance;

  4. validity period;

  5. limitations.

  1. Authentication shall remain separate from the Digital Signature creation process.

Article 9

  1. Where required by the applicable Profile, a Digital Signing Service shall require an Authorisation Outcome before initiating a signing operation.

  2. The Authorisation Outcome shall identify, where applicable:

  1. permitted signing operation;

  2. Actor;

  3. Subject;

  4. scope;

  5. validity period;

  6. restrictions.

  1. Authorisation shall remain separate from Digital Signature creation.

Digital Signature creation operation

Article 10

  1. A Digital Signing Service shall create a Digital Signature using the approved Digital Signature Creation Mechanism.

  2. The creation operation shall identify:

  1. data representation provided for signing;

  2. Digital Signature Creation Data reference;

  3. Digital Signature Creation Device reference;

  4. creation time;

  5. resulting Digital Signature.

  1. The Digital Signing Service shall preserve the relationship between the signing request and the resulting Digital Signature.

Article 11

  1. A Digital Signing Service shall produce creation evidence sufficient to reconstruct the Digital Signature creation operation.

  2. Creation evidence shall include, where applicable:

  1. signing request identifier;

  2. Digital Signature identifier;

  3. Digital Signature Creation Device reference;

  4. Digital Signature Creation Mechanism reference;

  5. creation time;

  6. service Version;

  7. applicable Profile.

  1. Creation evidence shall not expose Digital Signature Creation Data.

Service evidence

Article 12

  1. The Digital Signing Service shall maintain evidence sufficient to demonstrate operation of the service.

  2. Service evidence shall identify:

  1. received request;

  2. evaluation performed;

  3. dependencies used;

  4. creation operation;

  5. resulting Digital Signature;

  6. service outcome.

  1. Evidence shall be protected against unauthorised alteration.

Qualified Digital Signing Service

Article 13

  1. A Digital Signing Service intended to operate as a Qualified Trust Service shall satisfy the applicable Qualified Profile.

  2. The Qualified Profile shall identify:

  1. required Trust Service Provider Status;

  2. required Trust Service Status;

  3. applicable Digital Signature Creation Device requirements;

  4. applicable service assurance conditions;

  5. required evidence.

  1. Qualified Status of the Digital Signing Service shall not establish:

  1. Qualified Electronic Signature Status;

  2. Qualified Electronic Seal Status;

  3. Qualified Digital Signature Creation Device Status.

  1. Each qualified condition shall be evaluated separately.

Service lifecycle management

Article 14

  1. The lifecycle of a Digital Signing Service shall include, where applicable:

  1. preparation;

  2. activation;

  3. operation;

  4. modification;

  5. restriction;

  6. Suspension;

  7. cessation.

  1. Lifecycle events affecting signing operations shall be recorded.

Article 15

  1. Changes affecting the Digital Signing Service shall be assessed before implementation.

  2. The assessment shall consider:

  1. Digital Signature Creation Devices;

  2. Digital Signature Creation Mechanisms;

  3. supported Profiles;

  4. Authentication dependencies;

  5. Authorisation dependencies;

  6. Technical Specifications.

  1. Material changes shall be managed according to applicable Change Control requirements.

Incident management

Article 16

  1. A Digital Signing Service shall maintain procedures for:

  1. signing service interruption;

  2. Digital Signature Creation Device compromise;

  3. Digital Signature Creation Data compromise;

  4. failed signing operations;

  5. recovery.

  1. Incident records shall identify affected signing operations where applicable.

  2. The effect on created Digital Signatures shall be determined through applicable Validation processes.

Records and evidence

Article 17

  1. The Digital Signing Service shall maintain records sufficient to reconstruct:

  1. signing requests;

  2. authentication and authorisation dependencies;

  3. Digital Signature creation operations;

  4. service decisions;

  5. incidents;

  6. lifecycle changes.

  1. Records shall be protected according to applicable Security Conditions.

Applicable standards

Article 18

  1. The standards applicable to this Guideline are set out in Annex I.

  2. A standard referenced in Annex I shall apply only for the implementation function identified in that Annex.

  3. Conformity with a referenced standard shall constitute evidence only for the requirements mapped to that standard.

  4. A referenced standard shall not create:

  1. Electronic Signature Status;

  2. Qualified Electronic Signature Status;

  3. Controlled Effects.

Annex I

IDEHA-IG-SVC-SIG-001: Electronic Signature Service Implementation

Version: 0.1

Subject matter and scope

Article 1

  1. This Guideline lays down implementation requirements for Electronic Signature Services operating under the Trust Framework.

  2. This Guideline applies to Trust Service Providers providing Electronic Signature Services and Actors operating Electronic Signature Service functions within the applicable Service Scope.

  3. This Guideline establishes requirements for:

  1. Electronic Signature request processing;

  2. Signatory interaction;

  3. signing workflow management;

  4. signing intent evidence;

  5. presentation and confirmation of data before signing;

  6. delivery of Electronic Signatures;

  7. Electronic Signature service evidence.

  1. This Guideline applies together with:

  1. IDEHA-IG-OBJ-SIG-001 Electronic Signature Implementation;

  2. IDEHA-IG-OBJ-DSG-001 Digital Signature Creation Data and Device Implementation;

  3. IDEHA-IG-SVC-DSG-001 Digital Signing Service Implementation;

  4. IDEHA-IG-SVC-AUT-001 Authentication Service Implementation;

  5. IDEHA-IG-SVC-AUZ-001 Authorisation Service Implementation;

  6. IDEHA-IG-SVC-VVS-001 Validation and Verification Service Implementation;

  7. IDEHA-IG-ASR-GEN-001 Assurance, Conformity Assessment and Qualification Implementation.

  1. This Guideline does not establish:

  1. Digital Signature Creation Data requirements;

  2. Digital Signature Creation Device requirements;

  3. cryptographic algorithms;

  4. cryptographic parameters;

  5. Certificate issuance requirements;

  6. Digital Signature formats;

  7. Validation procedures.

Those matters shall be implemented through the applicable Framework Instruments.

Electronic Signature Service scope

Article 2

  1. An Electronic Signature Service shall operate within an identified Service Scope.

  2. The Service Scope shall identify:

  1. permitted Electronic Signature functions;

  2. supported Electronic Signature Profiles;

  3. supported signing workflows;

  4. applicable Authentication dependencies;

  5. applicable Authorisation dependencies;

  6. applicable Assurance Conditions;

  7. applicable Security Conditions.

  1. An Electronic Signature Service shall not perform functions outside its approved Service Scope.

Article 3

  1. An Electronic Signature Service shall maintain separation between:

  1. Electronic Signature workflow;

  2. Digital Signature creation;

  3. Authentication;

  4. Authorisation;

  5. Validation.

  1. An Electronic Signature Service shall not create legal effects beyond those established by the applicable Framework Instruments.

Electronic Signature request processing

Article 4

  1. An Electronic Signature Service shall process Electronic Signature requests according to the applicable Electronic Signature Profile.

  2. An Electronic Signature request shall identify, where applicable:

  1. requesting Actor;

  2. Signatory;

  3. data to be signed;

  4. intended purpose;

  5. applicable Signature Profile;

  6. required evidence.

  1. The Electronic Signature Service shall verify that the requested signing operation is within its Service Scope.

Article 5

  1. Before initiating a signing operation, the Electronic Signature Service shall determine that:

  1. the Signatory is identified according to the applicable Profile;

  2. required Authentication conditions are satisfied;

  3. required Authorisation conditions are satisfied;

  4. the data to be signed is identified;

  5. the signing workflow is applicable.

  1. The Electronic Signature Service shall not replace the Identification Service or Authentication Service.

Signatory interaction

Article 6

  1. The Electronic Signature Service shall provide mechanisms enabling the Signatory to participate in the signing process.

  2. The signing interaction shall ensure, where applicable:

  1. identification of the data to be signed;

  2. presentation of relevant signing information;

  3. confirmation of the signing operation;

  4. recording of the signing action.

  1. The applicable Profile shall define the required level of interaction.

Article 7

  1. The Electronic Signature Service shall ensure that the Signatory is able to understand the signing operation to the extent required by the applicable Profile.

  2. The signing interface shall identify, where applicable:

  1. signed data;

  2. relevant transaction information;

  3. signing context;

  4. applicable limitations.

  1. Presentation requirements shall remain separate from Digital Signature creation requirements.

Signing intent

Article 8

  1. Where signing intent is required by the applicable Profile, the Electronic Signature Service shall capture evidence demonstrating that the Signatory intended to apply the Electronic Signature to the identified data.

  2. Signing intent evidence may include:

  1. explicit confirmation;

  2. user interaction;

  3. transaction confirmation;

  4. another approved interaction mechanism.

  1. Signing intent shall remain separate from:

  1. Authentication;

  2. Authorisation;

  3. Digital Signature creation.

Article 9

  1. The Electronic Signature Service shall record signing intent evidence where required.

  2. The evidence shall identify:

  1. Signatory;

  2. signed data reference;

  3. signing event;

  4. time of confirmation;

  5. applicable workflow.

  1. Signing intent evidence shall be protected against unauthorised alteration.

Authentication and Authorisation dependencies

Article 10

  1. Where required by the applicable Profile, the Electronic Signature Service shall obtain an Authentication Outcome before completing a signing operation.

  2. The Authentication Outcome shall identify, where applicable:

  1. authenticated Subject;

  2. Authentication Service;

  3. Authentication Assurance;

  4. validity period;

  5. limitations.

  1. Authentication shall remain separate from the Electronic Signature.

Article 11

  1. Where required by the applicable Profile, the Electronic Signature Service shall obtain an Authorisation Outcome before completing a signing operation.

  2. The Authorisation Outcome shall identify, where applicable:

  1. permitted signing operation;

  2. Actor;

  3. represented Subject;

  4. scope;

  5. validity period;

  6. restrictions.

  1. Authorisation shall remain separate from the Electronic Signature.

Digital Signature service dependency

Article 12

  1. An Electronic Signature Service shall use a Digital Signing Service or equivalent Digital Signature creation function where a Digital Signature is required.

  2. The Electronic Signature Service shall maintain evidence of:

  1. Digital Signing Service used;

  2. Digital Signature creation operation;

  3. resulting Digital Signature;

  4. applicable Signature Profile.

  1. The Electronic Signature Service shall not modify the Digital Signature creation environment.

Article 13

  1. The Electronic Signature Service shall maintain the relationship between:

  1. Signatory;

  2. signing workflow;

  3. signed data;

  4. Digital Signature;

  5. resulting Electronic Signature.

  1. The relationship shall support Validation according to the applicable Profile.

Electronic Signature delivery

Article 14

  1. The Electronic Signature Service shall deliver the resulting Electronic Signature according to the applicable Profile.

  2. Delivery information shall identify, where applicable:

  1. Electronic Signature Identifier;

  2. recipient;

  3. delivery time;

  4. applied Profile;

  5. associated evidence.

  1. The delivered Electronic Signature shall remain protected against unauthorised alteration.

Qualified Electronic Signature Service

Article 15

  1. An Electronic Signature Service intended to provide Qualified Electronic Signatures shall satisfy the applicable Qualified Profile.

  2. The Qualified Profile shall identify:

  1. required Qualified Trust Service Provider Status;

  2. required Qualified Trust Service Status;

  3. required Digital Signing Service conditions;

  4. required Qualified Digital Signature Creation Device dependency;

  5. required Qualified Certificate dependency;

  6. required evidence.

  1. Qualification of the Electronic Signature Service shall not by itself establish Qualified Electronic Signature Status for every signature created through the service.

  2. Qualified Electronic Signature Status shall be determined according to the applicable Qualified Object Profile.

Service evidence

Article 16

  1. The Electronic Signature Service shall maintain evidence sufficient to reconstruct:

  1. signing request;

  2. Signatory interaction;

  3. Authentication and Authorisation dependencies;

  4. signing intent where applicable;

  5. Digital Signature creation reference;

  6. resulting Electronic Signature.

  1. Evidence shall be protected according to applicable Security Conditions.

Lifecycle management

Article 17

  1. The lifecycle of an Electronic Signature Service shall include, where applicable:

  1. preparation;

  2. activation;

  3. operation;

  4. modification;

  5. restriction;

  6. Suspension;

  7. cessation.

  1. Lifecycle events affecting signing operations shall be recorded.

Article 18

  1. Changes affecting an Electronic Signature Service shall be assessed before implementation.

  2. The assessment shall consider:

  1. applicable Electronic Signature Profiles;

  2. Digital Signing Service dependencies;

  3. Authentication dependencies;

  4. Authorisation dependencies;

  5. Technical Specifications;

  6. Security Conditions.

  1. Material changes shall be managed according to applicable Change Control requirements.

Accessibility and safeguards

Article 19

  1. An Electronic Signature Service shall provide Accessible Alternatives where required by the applicable Safeguard Conditions.

  2. Accessible Alternatives shall preserve the applicable Assurance Conditions.

  3. The applicable Profile shall define:

  1. assisted signing arrangements;

  2. alternative interaction methods;

  3. human support conditions;

  4. accessibility requirements.

Records and evidence

Article 20

  1. The Electronic Signature Service shall maintain records sufficient to reconstruct:

  1. signing requests;

  2. Signatory interaction;

  3. signing intent evidence;

  4. Authentication dependencies;

  5. Authorisation dependencies;

  6. Digital Signature creation references;

  7. service lifecycle events.

  1. Records shall be protected according to applicable Security Conditions.

Applicable standards

Article 21

  1. The standards applicable to this Guideline are set out in Annex I.

  2. A standard referenced in Annex I shall apply only for the implementation function identified in that Annex.

  3. Conformity with a referenced standard shall constitute evidence only for the requirements mapped to that standard.

  4. A referenced standard shall not create:

  1. Electronic Signature Status;

  2. Qualified Electronic Signature Status;

  3. Controlled Effects.

Annex I

Applicable standards

ETSI EN 319 401 General policy requirements for Trust Service Providers
ETSI EN 319 411-2 Qualified certificate issuing requirements where qualified signatures are supported
ETSI EN 319 102-1 Signature validation process requirements

ETSI EN 319 142-1 PAdES representation requirements
